newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Less poverty in Israel in 1995.
newsitem.headline: Less poverty in Israel in 1995.

text.p: The percentage of Israeli families defined as "poor" declined in 1995 for the first time in six years, according to an official report issued on Thursday.
"In 1995, for the first time since 1989, a decline was registered in the scope of poverty in Israel," said the report released by the Labour and Social Affairs Ministry.
"The percentage of poor families declined from 18 percent of all the families in 1994 to 16.8 percent in 1995," it said, relying on research conducted by the Central Bureau of Statistics.
A ministry spokesman said a family of four was defined as poor if its total monthy income was less than 3,071 shekels ($948).
The report said the financial situation of single-parent families had improved most in 1995, attributing it to an increase in government allowances for the poor.
The report added that other welfare reforms also contributed to the slight decline in poverty.
